newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Palm stresses stability after euro launch.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Palm stresses stability after euro launch.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Guntram Palm on Friday stressed the importance of maintaining solid fiscal discipline within the European single currency area after the planned launch of the euro in 1999.

In a summary of a speech to be delivered at a conference, Palm said the budgetary situation in 1997 was less important than the need to eliminate below-standard budgetary policies by individual member states in the currency union.
The decision on which countries will join the currency union from the start will be based on budget figures from 1997.
But lasting budgetary stability after the euro launch was even more important than convergence before the currency union starts, he said.

Palm also said convergence criteria had to be applied with strict stability in mind but that a "guillotine-like" application of limits referred to in the Maastricht Treaty would not make economic sense.
However, the use of one-off measures to get budget deficits in line would not suffice to prove stability.

The planned stability pact, which will impose sanctions on countries that fail to keep their finances in order after the euro is launched, should be as close as possible to the plans put forward by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel, Palm added.
He said the conditions under which a country could avoid sanctions ought to be defined far more restrictively and exactly.
